newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says satisfied with tin meeting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says satisfied with tin meeting.

text.p: Indonesia said on Thursday it was satisfied with the decision of the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC) to suspend export quotas.
The ATPC said at the end of a two-day meeting in Singapore on Tuesday that its supply rationalisation scheme would remain suspended for another year.

"We are satisfied with the results of the meeting because the ATPC in fact can still exist without economic provisions of the export quota system," Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, the director-general of mining, told reporters.
He said an ATPC subcommittee would meet in February to discuss the organisation's future.
"The subcommittee will meet in February to discuss the future of the ATPC. Indonesia sees that the ATPC can become a study forum for tin consumers and producers," he said.
The ATPC said 1995 tin exports by member countries totalled 100,023 tonnes, 10 percent higher than quotas set for the year.
The grouping also accepted the decision by Thailand and Australia to cease being members from December this year.
The ATPC links Bolivia, China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Nigeria. Zaire has stopped attending the grouping's meeting although it is still considered a member.
